title: AI Standardized Clients for Counseling Programs
one_liner: Voice-based AI 'clients' with persistent backstories, scored on accredited-skills rubrics, give master's students hundreds of rehearsal sessions before real practicum.
customer: Counseling, social-work and MFT master's programs (CACREP-accredited and similar), then OT and PT programs for patient-interview training; the department or a student lab fee pays.
problem: Practicum placements and faculty supervision are scarce. Human standardized clients cost about $30-60 an hour, and classmate role-plays are low fidelity. The new loan caps squeeze programs in excluded fields, and students need repetitions in high-stakes skills like suicide-risk assessment and motivational interviewing.
solution: Real-time voice client agents that stay consistent across sessions, remember last week, vary in difficulty and present safety-critical scenarios. Sessions are auto-scored on rubrics (reflective listening, risk questions asked, missed cues), supervisors review flagged clips, and sessions are logged as pre-practicum skills hours. Rehearsal volume is multiplied, not supervised hours replaced.
why_now: Low-latency, natural voice models with long-term memory reached usable fidelity in 2025-26. Programs in excluded fields face cost pressure after July 2026, and therapist demand remains strong.
revenue_model: $75-200 per student per semester as a lab fee, or $15-40k site licenses per program.
non_obvious_insight: What was infeasible was a client who stays consistent over sessions and reacts with emotion in real time. The binding constraint in clinical training is rehearsal volume, which is exactly what AI supplies cheaply, without threatening the human-supervised hours that licensure requires.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 counseling programs through adjunct faculty who teach skills labs. Build 6 scenarios (intake, motivational interviewing, suicide risk) and run a spring pilot. Measure improvement on the program's existing skills rubric and price at about $100 per student. Build in clinical safety review and privacy controls.

title: Vetted Remote Operators for Home Robots
one_liner: A privacy-audited, background-checked, insured pool of remote operators who take over home and warehouse robots at their hard moments, sold to robot makers as the trust layer for teleoperation.
customer: Home-robot, service-robot and warehouse-robot makers pay $18-35 per operator-hour. Operators are displaced support and ops workers earning $22-30 an hour.
problem: The first consumer humanoids (such as 1X's NEO) ship in 2026 relying on remote humans who can see inside homes, which raised a privacy backlash. Robot startups lack a scalable, vetted, insured operator workforce and would otherwise use anonymous offshore BPOs, while buyers want accountable domestic operators.
solution: Recruit and train from displaced call-centre, ops and gaming talent. A standard teleop certification, privacy protocols (blurred or avatarised feeds, no recording, no-go zones), session audit logs, background checks and E&O/cyber insurance form the service. Scheduling covers time zones and performance metrics track intervention success. Start with warehouse or delivery robots, then homes.
why_now: Consumer humanoid preorders and shipments began in 2025-26 with teleop as the fallback, warehouse and sidewalk robots are at scale, and privacy concerns make trust a differentiator.
revenue_model: 30-40% margin per operator-hour, certification fees and an insurance premium share.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck for robots is not hardware but trusted remote labor, and every teleop intervention also trains the policy. Privacy trust, not price, is the moat, and it reframes displaced workers as a new 'robot pilot' class.
first_30_days: Contact 20 robotics startups (delivery, warehouse, cleaning) with a pilot of 5 vetted operators for 200 hours at cost. Write the privacy protocol and audit template. Recruit 30 candidates from laid-off support and ops staff.

title: Displaced Insurance Agents Become Rooftop Solar Navigators
one_liner: Recruit the micro-agents wiped out by India's proposed insurance commission cuts as the trust-and-paperwork channel for rooftop solar, batteries and induction retrofits, paid per install by installers and lenders.
customer: MNRE-empanelled EPC installers and lenders (PSU banks, NBFCs) who pay per verified install or disbursed loan. The micro-agents (POSPs, motor-insurance agents, CSC operators) are the supply side.
problem: IRDAI's 2026-09-23 draft cuts general-insurance commission caps from 30% to 20%, sets 0% on motor third-party and 5% on own-damage, and PB Fintech fell 36% in one day. Hundreds of thousands of small agents in tier-2 and tier-3 towns lose most of their income. Meanwhile household solar and electrification demand is throttled by last-mile trust and paperwork (DISCOM feasibility, net-metering, subsidy claims, loans) rather than by hardware cost.
solution: A navigator app with training and payout rails. The agent walks a household through eligibility, vendor selection, DISCOM application, subsidy claim, bank loan and insurance for the new asset, earning per completed milestone. The annual motor-renewal touchpoint becomes the sales moment, and battery and induction bundles are added. The platform handles KYC, lead routing, quality control and payouts.
why_now: The IRDAI draft is days old and distributors such as PolicyBazaar and Turtlemint are squeezed and looking for new products. India's government-backed rooftop programs (verify current PM Surya Ghar terms) and LPG-shock induction demand are pulling households toward electrification, and UPI makes micro-payouts cheap.
revenue_model: INR 3,000-6,000 per installed home from the EPC (about 2-4% of net system cost), INR 1,000-2,000 per loan from lenders, insurance attach for the new asset, with the platform keeping 20-30% of bounties.
non_obvious_insight: Regulation just stranded a trusted, KYC'd, paperwork-fluent field force at the exact moment the bottleneck in electrification moved from hardware cost to last-mile trust. Insurance micro-agents are a distribution network searching for a product, and rooftop solar is a product searching for distribution.
first_30_days: Recruit 50 agents in one district through motor-insurance agent WhatsApp and Telegram communities and CSC networks. Sign 2 local EPCs on a per-commissioned-install bounty, run 20 installs end to end, and measure conversion from renewal touchpoints. Pay agents by UPI after commissioning.

title: Ticket Escrow Bot for Fan Communities
one_liner: A payment-escrow bot for the Discord, WhatsApp and Facebook groups where fans already swap tickets, releasing money only when a cryptographically verifiable ticket-transfer email arrives.
customer: Fans aged 18-35 (K-pop, pop tours, esports, festivals, football supporters) trading tickets peer-to-peer, and the community admins and moderators who police scams manually. Fans pay the fee, and admins get a revenue share.
problem: Ticket fraud thrives in fan groups because the only 'proof' is a screenshot, and generative AI now forges tickets, receipts and transfer confirmations trivially. Official resale is distrusted: per the briefing, Oasis tickets went from GBP 135 to 350+ under dynamic pricing, StubHub's World Cup 2026 tickets failed to reach buyers with class actions following, and the UK CMA ordered StubHub to refund 50,000+ customers over drip pricing. Fans therefore keep swapping in groups, where scammers pretend to transfer tickets or sell the same ticket several times.
solution: The buyer pays into escrow. The seller performs the official transfer in the ticketing app (Ticketmaster, AXS, Eventim, Fever and similar). The buyer sends the platform's 'tickets received' email to a unique escrow address, either forwarded as an .eml attachment or through a narrowly scoped read-only mailbox filter for that sender only. The system validates the DKIM/ARC signature, sender domain, event, section and seat lines, and that the recipient is the buyer, then releases funds after a hold for barcode rotation. Extras: automatic enforcement of a group's face-value cap, light seller verification above thresholds, an admin-facing reputation ledger, and cancellation refunds through an insurance partner. Payments run through a licensed platform-payments partner rather than holding funds directly.
why_now: AI-forged screenshots have made image evidence worthless. Per the briefing, Live Nation lost a federal jury verdict on monopolization in April 2026 and resale fees are under fire, the FTC's all-in pricing rule took effect in May 2025, and StubHub's delivery failures have left fans without a trusted route. Ticketing platforms increasingly move tickets by wallet transfer, so signed transfer emails are now standard.
revenue_model: 4-6% fee on escrowed amount, split between buyer and seller, with 0.5-1% shared with community admins. Premium 'insured swap' add-on. B2B API for promoters that want a safe official fan-swap channel.
non_obvious_insight: You do not need to beat Ticketmaster or become a marketplace. Every major ticketing platform already emits a DKIM-signed transfer email that is very hard to fake, a cheap trust anchor no fan-group scammer can produce. The distribution channel is community admins, who already do unpaid trust-and-safety work and will adopt anything that reduces their scam reports.
first_30_days: Pick one fandom with a high-volume swap group (a K-pop tour or a football supporters' group). Run concierge escrow by hand with a payments-platform account and a script that checks .eml DKIM. Handle 100 swaps at 5% and publish 'scams avoided' stats. Onboard 10 admin partners with a revenue share. Check ticketing terms of service per market before scaling.

title: Arc-Flash and Protection Studies Factory
one_liner: Deliver PE-stamped short-circuit, coordination and arc-flash studies in days rather than months, using AI to turn photos and one-lines into models.
customer: Electrical contractors and EPCs building C&I storage, EV depots and data center electrical rooms, plus facility managers facing five-year label refreshes.
problem: Power-systems engineers are scarce and studies gate energization and permits, with 8-12 week backlogs. A delayed 60 MW site costs about $3M a week. NFPA 70E requires reassessment every five years, and small C&I storage projects cannot afford $30k custom studies.
solution: Studies as a productized service. The contractor uploads single-line diagrams, nameplate photos and the utility fault-current letter. AI extracts the equipment and builds the ETAP or SKM model, a licensed PE reviews and stamps it, and the customer gets labels and coordination settings on a five-business-day SLA at a flat price per switchboard.
why_now: Vision and language models now parse one-lines and nameplates well enough to draft models. The data center and storage boom, and the engineer shortage, make throughput the scarce resource.
revenue_model: $3-15k per small C&I study, $30-100k per data center study, and recurring five-year renewals plus label printing.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody lacks software. They lack stamps and turnaround time. PE-supervised throughput with AI drafts is a labor arbitrage that stays unglamorous enough to avoid heavy competition.
first_30_days: Recruit two retired power-systems PEs. Build the extraction pipeline on 20 anonymized one-lines. Sell five C&I storage installers a $4k fixed-price study with a five-day SLA. Measure margins.

title: Metering Unmetered Wells From Orbit
one_liner: Estimate monthly pumping for every unmetered irrigation well by fusing radar subsidence, satellite crop water use and electricity data, and sell it to groundwater regulators.
customer: Groundwater sustainability agencies (about 140 in California), Texas groundwater conservation districts, Kansas management districts and Arizona active management areas, plus ag lenders, farmland funds and data-center developers relying on groundwater. Agencies pay annual fees.
problem: Most irrigation wells are unmetered, so regulators cannot enforce pumping limits or fees. Broad drought and Colorado River cuts push more pumping onto aquifers, and data centers in rule-of-capture states draw groundwater with little oversight.
solution: Fuse three signals: InSAR ground deformation (seasonal elastic movement tracks aquifer drawdown), ET-based irrigation demand minus effective precipitation, and pump electricity records from cooperating utilities. Calibrate against the wells that are metered and output pumping estimates with uncertainty per parcel and month. Deliver an evidence report agencies can use in fee and compliance programs.
why_now: The NASA-ISRO NISAR radar satellite launched in mid-2025 and its L-band data is open. ET datasets have matured. California's groundwater deadlines and the Texas audit push make measurement urgent.
revenue_model: $30-200k/yr per agency or basin, plus per-report fees to lenders and developers.
non_obvious_insight: Regulators do not need perfect meters, only defensible estimates calibrated against a sample of real ones, which is far cheaper than metering every well. The gap is that ET-only estimates cannot see storage change, and InSAR can.
first_30_days: Pick one critical-overdraft basin or Texas district with a metering plan. Reprocess two years of free Sentinel-1 InSAR, compare with the known meters, and publish a validation memo. Pitch three agencies on a 60-day paid pilot.

title: Seller-Brain Capture and Margin Leak Audit
one_liner: In the 90-day handover, reverse-engineer the retiring owner's pricing and rules of thumb from years of quotes and invoices, and find the contract and price leaks the seller never fixed, for a fee tied to recovered margin.
customer: First-time acquirers (search funders, independent sponsors, SBA-financed buyers, small holdcos) of $1-15M revenue service and light-manufacturing firms. SBA lenders and brokers are secondary referrers.
problem: The seller's pricing logic lives in his head, records are paper or Excel, and the handover is a 'handshake and good luck'. New owners find contractual minimums unbilled, price books frozen for years, parts sold below cost, and waste in telecom and software. They discover this only after closing, when the seller is already leaving.
solution: A 30-day sprint at signing or close. (1) Ingest 3 years of quotes, invoices, price books, contracts and vendor, phone and SaaS bills, including scanned paper. (2) An AI model reconstructs the implicit pricing rules and flags exceptions. (3) A structured, recorded 3-hour seller interview validates and labels the rules. (4) Output a working quote calculator, a written 'rules of thumb' manual, and a ranked leak list in dollars (unbilled contractual minimums, stale prices vs inflation, below-cost jobs and parts, dead subscriptions). The seller reviews the model weekly during the transition period.
why_now: Bain's 2026 reports say deals now need 10-12% EBITDA growth to hit returns and 79% of GPs expect flat purchase multiples, so operational upside has to be found rather than bought. Buyers of small firms feel the same pressure. LLMs now read messy PDFs, scans and Excel cheaply, which makes a 10-day audit cost a few hundred dollars in compute instead of a consultant's month.
revenue_model: $4-6K fixed fee for the capture sprint, plus 10-15% of annualized recovered margin in year one (capped). Optional pre-LOI 'upside memo' at $1.5-2.5K that buyers use to justify a bid and negotiate price.
non_obvious_insight: The leaks are contractual and forgotten, not strategic, and the seller's pricing logic is a perishable asset that expires with the transition period. Concrete cases from ETA operators: Tew & Taylor's contracts specified a two-hour minimum but the prior owner billed one hour, and after the buyer applied the contract rate there was 'virtually no customer pushback' (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/jack-rauch-tew-taylor). At Cardinal Heating & Air, prices were unchanged since pre-COVID, parts were sold below cost, and the buyer cut $1.4M of annualized cost in two weeks ($10K/month in cell phones vs $3K needed). Gross margins went from 7-20% to 48-49% (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/mike-bourgeois-cardinal-heating-and-air). At Winsor Fireform, pricing was the seller's 27 years of 'hunches', and the buyers 'sprinted' to extract it into a model during his 3-month transition; gross margin rose from 55% to 58-59% (https://acquiringminds.co/articles/andrew-sova-alex-clark-winsor-fireform-novo-foundry). At Gary Air, prices had not kept pace with inflation for 4+ years, and earnings went from $340K SDE to $1.3M EBITDA in 14 months (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/rob-brooks-gary-air). Four independent buyers found the same class of leak and each rebuilt it by hand.
first_30_days: Offer free audits to 10 first-time buyers found in ETA communities (Searchfunder, Acquiring Minds audience, ETA subreddits) in exchange for permission to publish anonymized before/after numbers. Build parsers for QuickBooks exports and for invoice exports from ServiceTitan, Jobber and Housecall Pro, plus a vendor-bill classifier. Create a one-page seller-interview protocol. Convert the first 3 free audits into case studies, then switch to contingency pricing.

title: Motor-Rewind Shops Become Drone-Motor Cells
one_liner: Qualify a network of existing U.S. electric-motor repair shops to wind and test compliant drone motors with non-Chinese magnets for Drone Dominance suppliers.
customer: Attritable-drone makers and tier-1 subsystem suppliers, including Gauntlet participants and Blue UAS suppliers. They pay per motor (about $60-150, my estimate, versus about $15-30 imported).
problem: The Pentagon's Drone Dominance Program targets more than 200,000 drones by 2027, and about 60,000 are to be ordered from Gauntlet 2 winners. At four motors per quadcopter that is about 240,000 motors for one tranche. China holds about 94% of magnet manufacturing, heavy rare earths stay tight through 2027, and capital is chasing airframes and software, not motors.
solution: Recruit motor-repair shops that already own winding skill, varnish and potting ovens, balancing and hipot test benches. Standardize a 'motor cell kit' (needle winders and fixtures, a single test spec, lot traceability logging) on a lease. The network operator holds customer contracts, source-verified magnet, bearing and lamination supply from domestic vendors, quality paperwork and DPAS-rated order handling, and passes work down. Each shop is audited like a franchisee.
why_now: Gauntlet cadence (roughly every six months) turns motors into a recurring bottleneck, and export controls make compliant sourcing urgent. Motor repair is a slow-shrinking industry, so shops have idle capacity. The Navy is retreating from early-stage funding, so distributed capacity without venture capital is the workable route.
revenue_model: 15-25% operator margin on motor sales, a $15-30k onboarding and equipment-lease fee per shop, and certification renewals. Later expand to ESCs, gimbals and wire harnesses using the same shop network.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is winding know-how and test discipline, not CNC capacity. Motor repair shops are typically classified as repair, so industrial-base maps built from manufacturing codes miss over a thousand of them. Hidden capacity, not new plants, is the fastest path to supply.
first_30_days: Contact regional chapters of the electrical apparatus service association to recruit 5 shops. Get 3 drone makers that currently fly Chinese motors to specify a compliant second-source design. Sell a prototype lot of about 500 motors with customer prepayment and run a first-article test.

title: Waste-Fat Origin Passports for 45Z Fuel
one_liner: Collector-level audits, chain of custody and lab fingerprinting that prove a load of used cooking oil or animal fat is North American.
customer: Renewable diesel, SAF and biodiesel producers, feedstock traders, and UCO collectors who want a price premium for proven origin.
problem: Since 2026, the 45Z clean-fuel credit has been limited to North American feedstocks, which creates an incentive to relabel imported UCO as domestic. Existing testing labs certify samples, not the collection chain, and producers face audit and credit-clawback risk.
solution: An 'origin passport' per load: KYC and site audits of collectors, GPS-tagged pickups, retained samples, and lab fingerprinting (fatty-acid and sterol profile, stable isotopes) against a growing reference library, delivered as per-load certificates and a traceability dashboard.
why_now: The 45Z origin restriction took effect for fuel made after 2025, so proof of origin has become a price factor. A UCO import surge and past fraud scandals mean auditors will look hard.
revenue_model: Per-load certificate fee of a few cents per gallon, annual collector audit fee, and subscription for producers.
non_obvious_insight: Waste is a fraud-prone commodity because the seller controls the paperwork. Verifying the collection chain, not the oil, is where enforcement will go.
first_30_days: Sign 2-3 mid-size collectors and one independent biodiesel producer as design partners. Build a reference sample library from those partners. Set up a lab partnership. Run first 20 loads with passports.

title: Rate-Leak Evidence Packs for Independent Hotels
one_liner: Mystery-shopping plus payout reconciliation that proves when OTA and reseller channels sold below the rate a hotel loaded, packaged as evidence for claims and regulator complaints.
customer: Independent hotels of 20-200 rooms in the EU, UK and US that rely on OTA merchant-model bookings, and hotel associations. The second buyer is a law firm or litigation funder that needs evidence to build a case.
problem: 51% of European hotels say OTAs sell below their loaded rate (up from 40% two years ago), Booking.com handles 66.1% of OTA bookings at surveyed hotels, and 26% of hotels do not know whether rates are passed on. A hotel loads $200, the guest sees $180, and the hotel is paid after checkout. Markups by Agoda, Citi, AA and Southwest loyalty portals are invisible to rate-shopping tools. The only party able to audit the markup is the one being audited.
solution: A panel of real-guest shoppers and reseller-portal quotes covers the hotel's next 90 dates. The results are reconciled against the hotel's folios and payout statements into a 'leak ledger' (date, channel, price shown vs loaded, payout). Timestamped, tamper-evident captures go into a monthly report and an evidence pack the hotel can hand to counsel, an association, a regulator (the EU DMA parity ban) or a claims funder.
why_now: The DMA (Booking designated a gatekeeper in 2024) bans parity clauses, so hotels have new legal options but no proof. The merchant model keeps growing. Fuel and energy shocks (Hormuz, March 2026) and a K-shaped market squeeze lower-tier independents, so recoveries matter.
revenue_model: About EUR 149 per property per month, plus a 20% contingent share of any recovery through a partner law firm or funder. Anonymized leak indices are sold to associations.
non_obvious_insight: The evidence does not exist until someone captures it in real time, and it is perishable because prices change hourly. The firm holding a year of timestamped leaks holds the case file, and OTA self-reporting can never be independent.
first_30_days: Partner with one regional hotel association (Spain, Italy or Croatia). Run a manual 30-date shop of Booking, Expedia, Agoda and two loyalty portals for 20 hotels, and deliver a one-page 'leak map'. Sell a one-off audit at EUR 300, convert 3-5 hotels to the subscription, and take the pack to one litigation funder as proof of concept.

title: Seasonal Staff Housing from Banned Rentals
one_liner: Master-lease flats stranded by short-term-rental bans and sublet them by the bed, with employer-guaranteed rent, to short-staffed hotels in the same destination.
customer: Hotels, resorts and restaurant groups with 50-400 seasonal staff in Palma, Ibiza, Barcelona coast and similar hotspots (start in the Balearics). Secondary customer: small owners whose licences are ending.
problem: Insiders frame STR bans as residents versus tourists, with owners as the losers. The overlooked fact is that banned owners have empty flats and fear 12-month tenancy law, while the hotel next door cannot hire because staff cannot find housing. Nobody sits in the middle to handle leases, furnishing, inspections and deposits.
solution: An asset-light intermediary signs 6-11 month leases with owners under a structure vetted by local counsel. The hotel guarantees the rent and places its own staff. We handle furnishing, house rules, inspections and optional payroll-deduction of rent, and charge per bed. The wedge is one Palma pilot with 3 hotels and about 30 flats.
why_now: Palma has a full ban, Barcelona bans all STRs in Nov 2028 after Spain's top court upheld it in Oct 2025, and Madrid restricts listings. Spain fined Airbnb $75M in Dec 2025, so the stranded supply is real. Spain still had about 97M visitors, so hotels are staffing to record demand.
revenue_model: A 12-18% management fee on rent, or a EUR 40-70 per bed per month spread, plus a placement fee from the hotel and a fee for guaranteeing rent to the owner.
non_obvious_insight: A ban strands supply as well as demand, and the best tenant for that supply is the employer of the people who service tourism. Employer-guaranteed rent is better credit than any nomad or mid-term tenant, which lets owners accept lower rents for zero vacancy risk.
first_30_days: Contact HR and operations heads at 15 hotels through the Mallorca hoteliers' federation and LinkedIn, and sign 3 letters of intent for 10-20 beds each. Recruit 30 owners through ex-STR property managers and owner groups. Pay a local lawyer EUR 3-5K for a lease template. Sign leases only after the hotel LOIs are in.

title: Recall-Proofing Subscription for Small Pet Food Brands
one_liner: Outsourced food-safety plans, pooled H5N1/Salmonella/Listeria testing and label review for the hundreds of small raw, freeze-dried and topper brands that cannot afford a QA department.
customer: Small raw, freeze-dried, topper and mixer brands and their co-packers, including Shopify-native brands.
problem: FDA now requires makers of cat and dog food using uncooked or unpasteurized poultry, dairy or egg ingredients to reanalyze their food safety plans for H5N1 under the animal-food preventive controls rule, after cats died from contaminated raw food. A recall can kill a small brand, and the fast-growing topper and mixer category (purchases +214% since 2018 per the briefing) creates label and 'complete and balanced' compliance ambiguity.
solution: A monthly subscription with PCQI-qualified plan writing and upkeep, supplier verification, a pooled testing program at negotiated lab prices with a certificate-of-analysis dashboard, mock-recall drills and label review against current AAFCO and state rules. Bundle with a recall-insurance partner for lower premiums.
why_now: FDA's H5N1 reanalysis requirement (announced January 2025) turned a news event into a permanent compliance line item. DTC consolidation (Farmer's Dog's first acquisition) raises supplier-diligence standards for small brands seeking exits.
revenue_model: $500-2,000 per month subscription, 20-30% margin on pooled testing pass-through, and insurance referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders treat H5N1 as an outbreak headline. For small brands it is a permanent, recurring cost, and testing volume can be pooled across many brands to get lab prices and QA depth no single brand can afford, the same economics that supports outsourced food-safety consultants in human food.
first_30_days: List 300 raw and freeze-dried brands from FDA registration and social listings. Send a free H5N1 gap audit against FDA's reanalysis requirement. Contract a PCQI consultant and one accredited lab. Convert 5-10 brands to paid subscriptions.

title: Hybrid-Race-in-a-Box Rentals for Gyms
one_liner: Rentable station kits, timing, waivers, insurance and sanitation protocols so any gym can run a Hyrox-style event for members.
customer: Independent gyms and CrossFit-style boxes (pay $2.5-4k per event); secondary: run-club organizers and corporate wellness days.
problem: Chain: Hyrox's global boom (events selling out, new markets such as Kuala Lumpur in December 2026) makes members demand local competitions, but official events are capacity-limited and licensed; local copycats need eight stations of gear, timing, heat management and a medical plan; and the Beijing incident (an athlete kept racing after soiling herself on shared equipment, prompting an apology and new biohazard rules) shows sanitation is a brand-level risk. Nobody sells a standardized, insured kit.
solution: A trailerized 8-station kit with standard loading specs, chip or QR bib timing through a phone app, wipe-down protocol cards and biohazard kit, medical response plan, waiver and event-insurance pack, and a results page. The gym sells tickets; we take rental plus a per-athlete fee.
why_now: Hybrid racing went mainstream in 2025-26, hygiene and safety incidents have made organizers seek documented protocols, and used sleds and ergs are cheap.
revenue_model: $2.5-4k per event rental plus about $5 per athlete for timing and insurance; sell kits to multi-gym operators at $18-30k.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not the format but the logistics and liability packaging for local operators; for a gym the payoff is member retention and lead generation from ticket buyers who are not yet members.
first_30_days: Buy $12-15k of used sleds, ballast and ergs, run a first event with a partner gym to document cost per athlete, offer three other gyms discounted rentals, and build a small QR-bib timing page.

title: Savings-Group Credit Score and Treasury
one_liner: Turn informal savings groups into a credit bureau and stablecoin treasury that asset financiers can lend against.
customer: Financiers of productive assets (solar irrigation, motorbikes, milk coolers) and NGOs, with savings groups as end users.
problem: Sandi AI already reaches 10,000+ farmer groups that buy solar irrigation from pooled savings rather than loans. Chamas, VSLAs, tandas and arisan have no records that lenders can see.
solution: A WhatsApp and USSD ledger that logs contributions and minutes, produces a group credit history and optionally holds a stablecoin group treasury that diaspora members can top up. The wedge is selling qualified-group leads to asset financiers.
why_now: Kenya and Nigeria are legitimising stablecoins, local-language voice models can log minutes, and Sandi AI has shown demand.
revenue_model: $20-60 per funded asset lead, plus a 0.5% treasury fee.
non_obvious_insight: The group is the unit of trust in informal finance. Digitising it creates a bureau that cannot be scraped from mobile money data.
first_30_days: Sign 100 groups in Kenya through one NGO and record three months of contributions to prove predictive value.

title: Reproduction-Gated Vulnerability Inbox for Maintainers
one_liner: A hosted security-report intake that only forwards a report if its proof-of-concept actually reproduces against the maintainer's tagged release in a sandbox, so AI-generated slop dies before a human reads it.
customer: Maintainers and foundations of widely depended-on open-source projects (paid by corporate sponsors and dependents), plus small vendors that must run a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy under the CRA. They pay $99-499/month per project, or $2k/month sponsor-funded shields for critical projects.
problem: curl ended its bug bounty at the end of January 2026 to 'remove the incentive for people to submit crap and non-well researched reports... AI generated or not'; in the week before, 7 submissions contained no real vulnerabilities but still burned security-team time. Maintainers are also drowning in PRs, with Ladybird banning non-maintainer PRs and Rust's Clippy gamifying review, while companies float donating AI credits to maintainers instead.
solution: An intake form and GitHub App that requires a machine-checkable reproducer (Dockerfile/script/HTTP request plus the expected oracle, such as an ASAN crash, unexpected file read or assertion). The service builds the project at the reported tag in a microVM, runs the reproducer and only escalates reports that trip the oracle. Failures get instant automated feedback. Passing reports arrive at the maintainer as a verified repro bundle, deduplicated against past reports, with a suggested severity and a drafted advisory and CVE request. Logic bugs without automatic oracles go through a refundable deposit lane. Start with memory-safety classes (C/C++/Rust/Go) where oracles are objective.
why_now: January 2026 made the AI-slop-versus-security-report problem concrete and public. CRA reporting duties began in September 2026, increasing report volume and the need for a documented intake. Cheap microVM sandboxes (Firecracker-class) make per-report verification cost cents.
revenue_model: Sponsor-paid subscriptions: $99-499/month per project, funded by the top dependents (companies that already say they want to help maintainers, per the AI-credits thread). $1-2k/month for critical projects. Per-verified-report fee for small vendors with public VDPs.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone argues about banning submissions or paying for them; nobody has moved the burden of proof onto machines, and the same LLMs that write slop cannot fake a crashing sanitizer trace on the maintainer's own build. The buyer is not the burned-out maintainer with no budget but the dependents who need that maintainer to keep going. Evidence: curl closing its bounty https://www.theregister.com/2026/01/21/curl_ends_bug_bounty/; maintainers asking how to handle PR slop and pointing to tools https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47492078; Ladybird and Clippy approaches plus a call for third-party solutions https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48949019; companies wanting to donate but debating the wrong instrument (credits vs money) https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48346013.
first_30_days: Build the GitHub App and intake page for C, Rust and Go projects using sanitizer/crash oracles. Recruit 3 mid-size maintainers by replying in the PR-slop and AI-contribution Ask HN threads; run their real inbox through it in shadow mode for two weeks and report the percentage of reports filtered. Take that data to each project's top corporate dependents and ask for a $250/month sponsorship that funds the shield.

title: Court-Safe Esper Machine From Bystander Video
one_liner: Blade Runner's Esper machine, made honest: a scaled, non-generative 3D reconstruction of an accident scene from mixed dashcam, doorbell, CCTV and phone clips, with error bars built to survive an admissibility challenge.
customer: Personal-injury law firms, insurer subrogation and special-investigation units, defense counsel and municipal risk managers, initially in disputed-liability vehicle and pedestrian cases with three or more video clips.
problem: Cases turn on several shaky clips. Traditional reconstruction by an expert costs thousands of dollars and takes weeks. Generative 'enhancement' gets challenged or excluded because AI invents pixels, and Gaussian-splat models look convincing but have no verified real-world scale.
solution: Ingest all clips, time-sync them (audio fingerprints, sirens, shared events), solve camera poses, and recover metric scale automatically from regulated-size objects in frame: lane-stripe cycles, stop and speed signs, crosswalk widths, license plates and standard curb heights. Output a measurable model with per-measurement error bars and a 'no generated pixels' guarantee (every pixel traceable to a source frame), plus vehicle speed and trajectory estimates and sightline views ('could the driver see the pedestrian?'). A partner licensed reconstructionist signs the report and serves as expert of record.
why_now: Feed-forward multi-view reconstruction and Gaussian splatting made casual-video reconstruction cheap in the last two years. Courts and defense bars are actively litigating AI-enhanced video. Doorbell, dashcam and storefront cameras mean most incidents now have several angles.
revenue_model: $900-2,500 per case, a discount tier for firms on subscription, and an expert-testimony fee split with the reconstructionist.
non_obvious_insight: Admissibility, not photorealism, is the product. Lawyers would rather have an ugly model with error bars than a beautiful hallucination, and automatic metric scale from objects whose dimensions are set by traffic-control standards is the unlock that separates this from generic splat tools and from drone-only videogrammetry.
first_30_days: Recruit one reconstructionist as expert of record. Offer 10 PI firms a free second-opinion reconstruction on live cases with at least three clips, then charge $1,200 for the next. Target five paying cases by day 90 and a written methods statement reviewed by a litigator.

title: Overtourism Feed for AI Travel Agents
one_liner: A destination-signed, machine-readable feed of live capacity, closures and dispersal incentives that AI trip agents query, so places can steer planning before tourists arrive.
customer: Destination management organisations and city tourism boards in overtouristed regions (Balearics, Dolomites, Kyoto, Lisbon, Dubrovnik, Amsterdam), later transport agencies and hotel groups.
problem: AI agents now plan and book trips (Booking.com and Expedia apps run inside ChatGPT), and they recommend the same hotspots blind to caps, closures and crowding. DMOs intervene only after arrival with fees and fines, which Venice's reportedly ineffective day-tripper fee shows is weak. Referral traffic from search is being eaten by AI answers.
solution: Publish an MCP server and JSON feed per destination with a daily load index by place and hour (from ticketing, parking, cruise calendars and occupancy), hard caps and permits, equivalent alternatives within about 60 minutes with partner lodging, resident-first hours and off-peak incentive codes. DMOs get a dashboard showing how many agent-planned trips shifted. Start with a hosted API and a DMO-embedded chatbot for immediate use.
why_now: OTA apps are now inside AI assistants, MCP servers are mainstream, booking lead times are shrinking, and AI overviews reportedly cut metasearch clicks by 31% in tested markets. DMOs need a way to influence the plan rather than the queue.
revenue_model: DMO subscriptions of EUR 20-100K per year, transparent sponsored 'dispersal' placements paid by under-visited partners, and analytics.
non_obvious_insight: Overtourism control is an information-timing problem. Influence must happen at itinerary generation, and AI agents are the first chokepoint where a single feed can shape millions of itineraries, giving destinations robots.txt-style power.
first_30_days: Build a feed for one region from public data (cruise schedules, park permit status, museum time slots) and ship the MCP server. Offer 3 DMOs a free traffic dashboard as design partners and embed it in their own website chatbots. Approach trip-planner app builders for consumption.

title: Outage Pucks: Street-Level Blackout Cover
one_liner: A $25 plug-in sensor that proves your power is out and triggers a cash payout after 12 dark hours, turning neighborhoods of pucks into their own insurance oracle and a data feed utilities will pay for.
customer: Small food businesses (corner stores, taquerias, bakeries, daycares, ghost kitchens) and households with power-dependent medical needs (home oxygen, CPAP, insulin fridges, breast-milk storage). Secondary buyers are utilities and municipal resilience programs.
problem: Outage losses (spoiled inventory, closed days, hotel stays) are small and frequent, and today they are effectively uninsurable. Utility tariffs limit liability, homeowners policies mostly ignore off-premises power failure, and no address-level proof of an outage exists, so no product can pay automatically.
solution: A cellular, battery-backed puck reports loss of mains power with tamper detection. Outages are confirmed by cross-verification when several pucks on the same feeder or block go dark together, plus utility outage feeds. Payouts are $100 at 12 hours and $100 per additional 12 hours up to $600, with a higher medical tier. The anonymized street-level outage map is sold to utilities, regulators and insurers.
why_now: Grid stress from aging distribution lines, surging data-center load and public safety power shutoffs in the West is a live concern for households and small businesses. LTE-M hardware is cheap and instant-payout rails exist. CPC/IRI's September 2026 outlooks show a very strong El Niño likely, which means an active southern storm track over California and the Gulf and Southeast this winter.
revenue_model: Puck-plus-cover subscription of $8-$12 per month, with premium share to the carrier/MGA. Data licensing to utilities and grid-resilience programs, and grant or utility-funded seats for medical-baseline customers.
non_obvious_insight: Crowd verification lets a device fleet act as a parametric oracle at a resolution utilities themselves lack on low-voltage segments, where they often learn of outages only when customers call. The insurance product pays for the sensor network, and the sensor network is the real asset.
first_30_days: Buy 200 off-the-shelf LTE-M power-loss sensors and firmware-tag them. Place them with a restaurant association and a home-health agency in one storm or shutoff-prone metro. Launch as a capped 'outage guarantee' service warranty from the company's own balance sheet while an MGA is lined up. Pitch the aggregated outage map to one utility resilience team.

title: Result-Loop Desk for Scan and Lab Startups
one_liner: An outsourced nurse-and-radiologist desk that closes the loop on abnormal results from full-body scans, MCED tests and mega-panels.
customer: Mid-tier consumer diagnostics operators without downstream care: full-body MRI resellers, regional imaging centers, longevity clinics, mega-panel labs and employer executive-health programs.
problem: A review of 12 studies found 95% of asymptomatic people had at least one abnormal whole-body MRI finding and 91% of those were not clinically relevant (15-30% false-positive rate). Primary-care waits average ~31 days, so patients arrive at their PCP with printouts. Adoption is accelerating (Neko $700M for a NYC launch, Function 1M+ members), and Lp(a) testing hit a wall when Lp(a)HORIZON failed on Sep 4, 2026, leaving many flagged people without a next step.
solution: Triage each flagged result (ignore, repeat in X months, refer), track follow-up imaging against nodule and lesion guidelines, produce a structured PCP handoff (FHIR), document loop closure and route to a price-transparent cash referral network. Sold as a risk-management service. Consumers can buy a $99 second-opinion review.
why_now: Elective screening boomed in 2025-26 (Function-Ezra, Neko US launch, MCED tests despite NHS-Galleri missing its primary endpoint in May 2026). Medscape and radiology press now describe a 'medical cascade', so reputation and liability risk are becoming visible to operators.
revenue_model: $40-150 per flagged member (B2B), plus annual tracking fee per incidental finding, plus consumer second-opinion upsell.
non_obvious_insight: Screening companies are paid at the scan, but the costs of false positives and lost follow-ups land months later on nobody. Because they are not care providers, they cannot build the follow-up function in-house, so it converts to a compliance product.
first_30_days: Sell a pilot to three regional imaging centers or longevity clinics that resell whole-body MRI. Staff one part-time radiologist and one RN navigator, run follow-up tracking with SMS and a spreadsheet, and charge $75 per flagged patient. Publish a 'follow-up leakage' audit as the sales asset.

title: Harvest-Season Fab Van for Farm Machinery
one_liner: A trailer with industrial printers, a small mill and lathe, and a 3D scanner that parks at grain co-ops during harvest and planting and fabricates the broken part while the farmer waits.
customer: Row-crop and specialty farms, custom harvesters and independent ag-repair shops (Midwest, Plains, Central Valley), plus farm co-ops that host the van.
problem: A combine or planter is worth thousands of dollars a day inside a 10-day weather window. The dealer's part is backordered, discontinued or priced like a ransom. The failed item is usually a $3 plastic or steel piece: a latch, bracket, sensor mount, cab trim, bushing, pin, wear pad or knob.
solution: Two things. First, a mobile print-and-machine unit (carbon-fiber nylon printing, benchtop CNC mill and lathe, handheld scanner) that turns a broken part into a fabricated one in hours. Second, a growing digital parts library indexed by machine make, model and serial number, where every repaired part becomes a reusable file. Farmers can also buy a 'Season Pass' per machine that guarantees fabricated-part turnaround inside 24 hours.
why_now: The FTC and five states settled with Deere on July 8, 2026. For 10 years Deere must give farmers and independent shops the same repair software and resources it gives dealers, and it separately agreed to a $99M class settlement. That will grow independent repair shops, and parts are the next bottleneck. Crop margins are tight, so cheaper aftermarket parts sell, and harvest is happening right now.
revenue_model: Per-part fabrication ($40 to $600, with a rush premium), Season Pass subscriptions ($1k to $2.5k per machine per season), wholesale to independent repair shops, and a co-op hosting fee or revenue share.
non_obvious_insight: Farmers don't buy parts. They buy hours inside a weather window, so price against downtime avoided, not material cost. The scanned-part library by machine serial number is the compounding moat. Every emergency job builds the catalog that later lets you ship parts remotely, and the van is really a data-acquisition vehicle.
first_30_days: Borrow or rent a machine shop and start with two industrial printers, a benchtop mill and a scanner (about $40k to $60k), or begin with a used trailer. Sign two independent ag-repair shops and one co-op as hosts. Run a 'we fix it while you wait' pilot through the rest of this harvest, charging from job one. Post before/after photos in local farm Facebook groups and to elevator and co-op newsletters. Log every part as a file.

title: Conversion X-Ray: Scan and Warrant Hidden Risks
one_liner: A 10-day scan of vacant office buildings (LiDAR, ground-penetrating radar, riser mapping) with an AI cost-risk budget, evolving into a cost-overrun warranty backed by the data.
customer: Buyers of distressed office evaluating conversion, their construction and mezzanine lenders, and later sureties and insurers.
problem: Conversions fail on unknowns: slab thickness and post-tension cables, asbestos and fireproofing, riser locations, window operability, structural transfers. Buyers price with averages and blow budgets by 20-40%, and lenders demand large contingencies or refuse.
solution: A rapid package for 40-300k sf buildings: handheld or drone LiDAR, GPR on slabs, facade thermal imaging, MEP riser mapping and sample testing. An AI cost-risk model outputs a per-unit cost distribution and a P80 budget in 10 days. As actual-versus-predicted data accumulates, offer a warranty or overrun cover.
why_now: $39B of office debt matures within 12 months and the buyer pool needs faster diligence. Handheld SLAM LiDAR and vision models are cheap, and public-land and affordable conversions require cost certainty.
revenue_model: $0.30-0.90 per sf for the scan, later warranty premiums of 1-2% of hard cost or lender-paid programs.
non_obvious_insight: Every conversion overrun is a data point that nobody collects. The first firm to log predicted-versus-actual cost across 50 conversions owns the only actuarial dataset in a market that insurers cannot yet price, so the scan is the loss leader for an insurance-like margin.
first_30_days: Buy a handheld LiDAR and rent a GPR unit. Scan three buildings at a discount for buyers in bid periods. Publish 'the top 10 hidden conversion killers' and sign two paid scans at about $15K each.

title: Universal Depot Operator for Stacked EPR Programs
one_liner: One neutral drop-off depot per town that serves batteries, paint, oil containers, textiles and small e-waste for many producer responsibility programs at once.
customer: PROs and stewardship programs (Circular Action Alliance, battery, paint and other stewardship organizations) under a master service agreement, plus host sites paid a host fee.
problem: EPR programs multiply, each building its own thin collection network. Colorado's Interchange 360 (petroleum containers) diverted about 2,500 lb in six months across 10 collection facilities, roughly 250 lb per site. Unit costs per pound are absurd, host sites drown in per-program rules, and households face a different trip per program.
solution: A shared depot at transfer stations and hardware stores with one trained staff, fire-safe cabinets and one weekly consolidated pickup. It is operated under a multi-PRO contract paid per pound plus a site fee. It starts in Colorado and Oregon and adds streams as new programs launch (California's SB 501 medium-format batteries, textiles).
why_now: Colorado's programs are just moving from planning to practice. Oregon's EPR survived the Commerce Clause challenge (Aug 2026) even as NAW appeals, and CAA collected $145.5M in 2025 while spending $56.5M, so budget exists to solve collection cost.
revenue_model: Per-lb handling fees and per-site fees from multiple PROs, host-fee share, and minor resale of recovered commodities.
non_obvious_insight: EPR is designed by material stream but households experience it by trip. The missing layer is a neutral aggregator that turns N programs into one drop-off and one truck.
first_30_days: Meet PRO operations leads in Colorado and Oregon. Pick 3 host sites in one county (a transfer station and 2 hardware stores). Price cabinets and a pickup route. Sign one PRO pilot on cost-plus terms.

title: Circle Cue: Name Whispers for Early Dementia
one_liner: Consent-only Bluetooth badges let earbuds whisper who a person is and one line of context to someone with mild cognitive impairment, with no cameras and no face recognition.
customer: Families of people with mild cognitive impairment or early Alzheimer's ($149 kit plus $15 a month), memory cafes, senior centers and faith groups, and later Medicare Advantage plans and dementia-care programs.
problem: People in early dementia often withdraw because forgetting names is humiliating, and caregivers watch the social world shrink. Face-recognition glasses are legally and ethically fraught (biometric-privacy laws), and dementia technology focuses on safety tracking rather than social participation.
solution: Circle members (family, neighbors, club regulars) opt in by wearing small Bluetooth badges with rotating IDs. The user's phone detects nearby IDs and whispers, for example, 'Tom Reyes, your neighbor; knee surgery last month' from a one-line card written by the circle and managed by the caregiver. It works offline and cards expire to avoid stale information.
why_now: Cheap BLE, on-device speech and summarization, and LE Audio earbuds make this cheap to build. FDA-cleared Alzheimer's blood tests (2025) and anti-amyloid drugs are pushing diagnosis earlier, creating a fast-growing population that is cognitively capable and socially at risk for years.
revenue_model: Hardware kit, monthly subscription, and B2B circle licenses for memory cafes and senior centers. Later: plan-funded coverage.
non_obvious_insight: The privacy-safe alternative to face recognition is consent by badge: a small, fully opt-in social graph of 10-30 people that covers most of what the person meets each week. Consent is the feature, and it turns surveillance tech into hospitality.
first_30_days: Partner with three memory cafes. Make 30 badges (about $4 each) and a prototype app. Trial with five families free, measure outings per week before and after, then sell $149 kits.

title: Buildings-as-Mines Salvage Reserve Reports
one_liner: Mining-style reserve estimates for buildings before demolition, built from phone LiDAR and AI that reads the drawings, then a market for pre-sold salvage rights.
customer: Demolition and selective-strip contractors and developers doing office-to-residential conversions (first), later scrap buyers, banks and salvors.
problem: Demolition bids depend on a walk-through guess of salvage value in copper, aluminum, steel, glass and fixtures. Contractors overpay or underbid, and no one sells forward the metals inside a building, unlike any mined commodity.
solution: A 48-hour reserve report with tonnage, value and confidence bands (P10/P50/P90). It uses LiDAR and thermal scans, stud and cable finders, and an LLM that reads as-builts and MEP drawings. A bid-day marketplace lets salvage buyers commit. Long term, salvage-rights forwards on the building stock.
why_now: Phone LiDAR and models that can read drawings became good enough in 2025-26, at a time when office conversions are surging and metal prices are elevated.
revenue_model: $1.5-5K per report, plus 3-5% of salvage value transacted through the marketplace.
non_obvious_insight: Demolition is the only mining-like business with no reserve estimate. Once a reserve report exists, salvage rights become financeable and pre-sellable.
first_30_days: Scan 10 buildings free with a partner contractor, then back-test estimates against actual scale tickets. Sell the first reports at $1,500 to 5 contractors.

title: Orphaned Solar Lease Cleanup at Home Closings
one_liner: A closing-desk service that untangles orphaned solar leases, PPAs and UCC fixture filings on retirees' homes so sales and estates can close.
customer: Title and escrow companies, listing agents, elder-law attorneys and estate executors, who pay per closing (fee taken from sale proceeds). Secondary customers are the retired homeowners themselves and their adult children.
problem: Door-to-door and telemarketed solar leases and PPAs were sold at kitchen tables to retirees on 20-25 year terms. Each one usually leaves a UCC-1 fixture filing on the home. The lessor may since have gone bankrupt (Sunnova filed Chapter 11 in June 2025 and its portfolio was sold and is now serviced by SunStrong; Mosaic and Sunlight failed earlier). Sales stall at the last minute because the buyer's lender wants the lease assumed or paid off and nobody can find the assignment chain, the current servicer or a payoff quote. Heirs inherit a lease on a dead parent's house, with monitoring dead and inverters failing. Homeowners rarely have copies of what they signed.
solution: A fixed-scope workflow. (1) Pull county and state fixture filings and reconstruct the chain of assignment. (2) Identify the current servicer and pull the contract. (3) Produce either a lender-ready transfer/assumption package with the buyer's credit-approval prep, or a payoff/buyout quote. (4) File the lien release. (5) Where the sales pitch looks deceptive or the lease unenforceable, hand off to a consumer attorney. A shared database of lessor entities, servicers and their turnaround times compounds as more closings run through it. The service is priced so title companies see it as saving their fee on a dying deal.
why_now: The Sunnova bankruptcy (filed June 2025, plan effective November 2025) created a live wave of stuck transfers, and multiple state AGs are investigating. The federal homeowner solar credit ended after 2025, pushing installers toward leases and PPAs, which let the company keep the tax credit. Leases signed in 2016-2020 are now reaching resale and probate age as the peak-65 cohort dies or downsizes.
revenue_model: Flat $750-$1,500 per closing, paid at settlement from proceeds. Title companies can take a $299/month priority-handling subscription. There is an optional buyout-negotiation success fee, and attorney referral fees where the state allows.
non_obvious_insight: The panels are not the blocker. The blocker is paperwork nobody can find: a recorded fixture filing and an assignment chain across three companies. Closers know it as the #1 surprise at the eleventh hour. Half the street signed in 2017 with a clipboard salesman and kept no copies. Whoever owns the lessor and servicer map, and the county filing pipeline, owns the unblock.
first_30_days: Pick one high-solar county in TX, FL, CA or AZ. Scrape recorded fixture filings by known lessors and cross-match them against new listings and probate filings. Call 15 title offices that have had a stuck solar closing and offer the first 3 at cost. Build template packages for the top 5 lessors and servicers. Partner with one elder-law attorney and one consumer-protection lawyer for hand-offs.
